context: Review finding on fix/repo-ids CONFIRMED, not refuted: a store that ran identity init and was then migrated by a pre-591fcf63 `migrate --to 3` keeps the path-seeded store_id/repo_id on every rerun (resolveIdentity returns legacy/migration-state.json's identity first; finalize can only union ids the CURRENT store.json declares, and the init ids were overwritten out of it). Reproduced on the fixed code by moving the init descriptor aside for the first run (the seed is the store path, so the pair is the one the old code minted) and pinned as a test in test/migrate/v3-identity-reuse.test.ts. No heal path added — the reviewer's own fix says none is required for this commit and the heal is a design choice (see decisions). Applied the exact detection the reviewer asked for: `twining doctor` now reports bindings.repo_ids_cited (every scope.repo the journal cites), bindings.repo_ids_undeclared (cited but absent from store.json repo_ids) and an honest_limits line naming the ids when the set is non-empty; two doctor cases added in test/cli/v3-verbs.test.ts. resolveIdentity's doc comment names the limitation. Tests: v3-identity-reuse 5/5, v3-verbs 27/27, tsc clean.
rationale: that branch is checked out in worktree wf_7fdd8f5c-571-1, so git refuses a second checkout; the caller fast-forwards fix/repo-ids to the reported sha. The task's literal recipe (branch from fix/working-set-render) would have dropped the fix commit the finding is about, so it was read as a template and the fix tip used instead.
summary: Chose branch fix/repo-ids-review (from 591fcf63, the fix/repo-ids tip) in this worktree rather than fix/repo-ids
